## COORD — Coordinating work

→ [standard](standards-coordination.md)

The territory work and Project work a repository shows in its work files, with old-shape checkpoints for the tolerance window, and the responsiveness, reporting and currency of the coordinators behind them.

- **COORD-1 [M] — territory work belongs to the Capital** — A territory Capital, a repository whose declared `capital` is itself, holds its territory work, `+/_WORK/<territory>.sop.main/work.md`, retaining legacy `<territory>` input indefinitely, titled `<Territory> > SoP`, and no other repository holds territory or Project packages; deliberately owner-approved regular/ad hoc member work declares Home: in work.md Scope, and its parent maintains the existing covers/home reference without a second package. Regular umbrella and child packages remain eligible; coverage never opens coordination. For the tolerance window a Capital whose territory work is still the state-of-play checkpoint `+/_CHECKPOINTS/_state-of-play.md` passes with a warning naming its new home. (standards-territory.md#territory-work, standards-coordination-migration.md#thread-model)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Create the territory work package in the Capital under the `ki-work-package` work-package standard, or move the state-of-play checkpoint there at the territory's migration, and remove territory work from any repository that is not its own capital.
- **COORD-2 [M] — Project work resolves in the registry** — Each Project work file `+/_WORK/<territory>.prj.<project>/work.md` names its `project`, its title ends in that Project's title, as in `KI > Model > Ways of working`, and on a Capital its Project resolves in `Streams/Projects/` and any `theme` in `Streams/Themes/`; a theme resolving only in the legacy `Streams/Initiatives/` warns, naming its new page, until 2026-11-07 and fails from that day. For the tolerance window an `<initiative>.<project>.md` checkpoint is checked as before, its label ending in its Project's title, or its slug in words where the Project note has no title, and its Initiative resolving in `Streams/Initiatives/`, with a warning naming its new home. (standards-opening.md#work-naming, standards-territory.md#coordinating-work)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Correct the work file's `project`, `theme` or title at its next update, or register the Project or theme under the `ki-work` registry standard.
- **COORD-10 [M] — work files declare a level that agrees with their id** — Each work file declares its `level`, which agrees with its id: `sop` names territory work (`main` or a named secondary), `prj` names Project work and `reg` names regular work (legacy `regular` stays readable); legacy one- and two-part names stay readable indefinitely. For the tolerance window the `_state-of-play.md` checkpoint carries `role: state-of-play` and each `<initiative>.<project>.md` checkpoint `role: coordination`, or `role: conversational`, and no other checkpoint declares `state-of-play`. (standards-opening.md#levels-and-forms)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Have the work correct its `level`, or an old-shape checkpoint its `role`, at its next update, or ask by a line in its `messages.md`; never edit another piece of work's front matter to change it.
- **COORD-3 [M] — active Project work is within the cap** — At most three or four pieces of Project work are active at once, neither On hold nor Finished, reading the state from `state.md` where the work package has one, counting old-shape coordination checkpoints whose state is active; territory work, regular work and work awaiting review in `+/_WORK_REVIEW/` are not counted, and a non-empty `+/_WORK_REVIEW/` warns so that territory work raises it as one `REVIEW-HOLD` query. Under the owner-queue cap, more than eight roadmap records with `status: awaiting-review` naming a piece of Project work's Project also warn, counted in the checkout and in each checkout beside it that names the same Capital. (standards-territory.md#territory-work)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Have territory work put Project work on hold or queue it until the active list is within the cap; exceeding that active Project cap requires explicit owner agreement beforehand, never a unilateral increase; over eight records awaiting acceptance, launch no new build or planning run until acceptance catches up, keeping acceptance fixes and backlog-clearing work.
- **COORD-7 [M] — every record identifier in a work report is a link** — In every report in a work folder, in each focus folder its `work.md` declares, `+/_WORK/<id>/<focus-id>/*.report.md`, and in `+/_WORK/<id>/reports/*.report.md`, and for the tolerance windows in every report still at a work folder's top level and every thread report `+/_THREADS/<run>/*.report.md`, each full record identifier in the prose, a work record such as `KI-HARNESS-GOV-187` or a Decision Record such as `ADR-KI-HARNESS-010`, sits inside the text of a Markdown link, and a link that names a record and targets an absolute local path points at a file that exists, inside the audited checkout or wherever the target's folder is present on the machine; a target outside the checkout whose folder is absent, as on a CI runner, is checked for shape only, a Markdown file name opening with the linked identifier; a pruned record is linked as `<FULL-ID> (pruned)` to the GitHub link to the file at its last revision. Fenced blocks, such as a past reply block, inline code spans, which quote literal text such as a commit subject, and Needs tags such as `ACCEPT-181` are not checked; work awaiting review is not checked. (standards-reporting.md#linking-records, standards-coordination-migration.md#coord-7-and-thread-folders)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Make each bare identifier the text of a link to its record by absolute path; where the record has been pruned, link it as `[<FULL-ID> (pruned)](https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<last revision>/<path>)`. Fix only the reports of the work under review.
- **COORD-11 [M] — every recommended option in a work report carries its confidence** — In every report under `+/_WORK/<id>/` or `+/_THREADS/<run>/` whose form line leads with a glyph state, or whose block-letter footer was issued on or after 2026-10-18, each line of its Queries section that marks a lettered option recommended, `<letter>) (recommended`, reads `<letter>) (recommended, confidence high|medium|low - <reason>)`, and no `###` query marks more than one option recommended. A report issued earlier, or with neither to date it, and fenced blocks are not checked. (standards-reporting.md#owner-report, standards-queries.md#query-review, standards-coordination-migration.md#coord-11-confidence-cutover)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Give each flagged option its confidence and a one-line reason, never `high` for a destructive course resting on claims not verified directly; split a query that recommends more than one option into separately tagged queries. Fix only the reports of the work under review.
- **COORD-12 [M] — every work report opens with its report heading** — Every report under `+/_WORK/<id>/` or `+/_THREADS/<run>/` has the `#` report heading as its first non-blank line, or, for a report saved with front matter, the front matter first and the heading as the first non-blank line after it. A frame rule, a lint directive or a form line before the heading does not pass. Work awaiting review is not read. (standards-reporting.md#owner-report, standards-report-forms.md#report-forms)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Move the report heading to the top of each flagged report, after its front matter if it has any, before the work is marked or sent. Fix only the reports of the work under review; other work fixes its own before its next mark.
- **COORD-8 [M] — the coordinator hook and output style are bound where ki-coordination is declared** — In the runtime-specific Claude Code binding, a repository that declares `[skills.ki-coordination]` selects `"outputStyle": "ki-coordinator"` in its tracked `.claude/settings.json`, and, where the user's Claude Code settings are present, they run the harness `hooks/coordinator-reminder/coordinator-reminder.sh` at `UserPromptSubmit` and `SessionStart` and the style is deployed as `~/.claude/output-styles/ki-coordinator.md`. The user-environment manager, chezmoi, stays the binder; the rubric only checks that the binding is present. (standards-coordination.md#coordinator-responsiveness)
  - _Remediation:_ diagnostic — Select the output style in the repository's tracked `.claude/settings.json`; bind the hook and deploy the style through the user-environment manager, such as `chezmoi apply` after reviewing `chezmoi diff`, rather than by editing user settings by hand.
- **COORD-4 [J] — coordinators stay responsive and work stays current** — A coordinator never does substantive work itself, sends every unit of work to a detached background agent and treats an owner message as steering rather than a stop; each turn makes at most five tool calls with reads limited to the work package, one read of its files counting as one call, `ki agent status`, one report and one short file and writes limited to the work package, the decisions log and a brief, waits only through a detached waiter or monitor, keeps a background check armed while work lies with a worker that wakes it only when a run finishes, with no timed bound and no timed update while it waits, with no heartbeat otherwise, keeps one inbox watcher armed only when the owner has asked the thread to listen, or it is a Rig host sync thread, and the work is not draining, On hold or Finished, that silently fetches and fast-forwards and wakes it only on a new message line or a finished run, shows a listening or sync mode line in the banner only while that mode is on, acts on new `messages.md` lines at each wake in queue order, important lines first, answers owner messages within one short turn and reports drift in one line; each territory Capital has one main State of play coordinating registered Project packages within its cap, through explicit committed assignment and acknowledged handover of in-flight runs without timeout takeover; the assignment field remains undecided. It acts in one assigned package per turn, keeps the queue and seeds each work folder and opener, and any secondary State of play names the main as `parent`, lists the work it `covers` and routes cross-cutting matters to the main, which stays the front door for the owner; Project work works only its Project, follows the bootstrap, keeps its state file current and records approvals before launching; a routed line is never rejected whole, only the part not its own returned once to the State of play that routed it. (standards-coordination.md#coordinator-responsiveness, standards-listening.md#inbox-watch, standards-territory.md#coordinating-work)
  - _Evidence scope:_ Coordinator transcripts, work packages, decisions logs and summaries the owner selects for review.
  - _Review prompt:_ Did the coordinator keep within five tool calls a turn, delegate rather than analyse, draft, edit, test or wait in the foreground, issue no command that may wait for a permission prompt, such as an `rm` with a glob, variable or `$(...)` target, `git worktree remove` or a foreground `sleep` of 60 seconds or more, give timed updates only when work launched or a run finished, with no timed wake or update while waiting, keep the inbox watcher armed only when the owner had asked the thread to listen, or it was a Rig host sync thread, and the work was not draining, On hold or Finished, show a listening line in the banner only while listening, answer owner messages within one short turn and stop work only on an express, named instruction, does territory work stay on project management with active Project work within the cap and a prepared work folder and opener for each, and does each piece of Project work run through background agents from a current state file, taking its message queue in priority order?
  - _Outcomes:_ conforming; delegate longer work; escalate to owner
  - _Conforming guidance:_ Move longer coordinator work into background agents and note the drift in the state file; escalate to territory work when a direction touches more than one Project.
- **COORD-5 [J] — coordinators park tangents, link records and keep checkouts current** — A coordinator parks passing side topics as dated one-line items under `discussions.md`'s `## Parked`, cites and links every record, work file, theme and Project by full identifier and local path, and fast-forward pulls affected clean primary checkouts after background agents push. Commit each complete unit and finished package change by explicit path before its turn ends; sync after each finished change and at least every 15 minutes. Push everything stacked on main, including other sessions' commits, fast-forward only, never forced or with --no-verify, stopping on divergence. Conflict repair belongs to a bounded isolated run that rebases only this work's unpublished commits and stops on other content, uncertain ownership or judgement. (standards-mark.md#parking-tangents, standards-reporting.md#linking-records, standards-sync.md#keeping-primary-checkouts-current)
  - _Evidence scope:_ Coordinator transcripts, status lines, reports, summaries and work files the owner selects for review.
  - _Review prompt:_ Were side topics parked without derailing the work and later homed or dropped, does every mention of a record, work file, theme or Project carry its full identifier and a local link, and are the owner's primary checkouts current, with dirty or diverged ones reported rather than altered? Were completed package changes committed promptly, was the 15-minute sync floor met, and did any conflict run stay within those ownership and authority boundaries?
  - _Outcomes:_ conforming; park or home tangents; fix references; refresh checkouts; escalate to owner
  - _Conforming guidance:_ Move tangents into `discussions.md`'s `## Parked` or their proper home, replace short or unlinked references with full identifiers and local paths, and fast-forward only clean checkouts; report a dirty or diverged checkout to the owner instead of repairing it.

- **COORD-13 [J] — coordinators have doubtful and destructive queries reviewed blind** — Before a query reaches the owner, a coordinator sends every query whose recommended option carries `medium` or `low` confidence, and every `high` one whose course destroys, deletes or publishes, to one blind review run on the strongest model at high effort, under Codex rather than Claude Code where independence matters; agreement lifts the confidence one level, never to `high` for a destructive course resting on claims not verified directly, with its reason beginning `reviewed`, and disagreement keeps the confidence, begins the reason `review disagrees` and shows both views in the query. The review brief carries the review-independence sentence and states earlier decisions as dated facts, and a review that challenges an earlier decision is shown at the end of the Context with an option to revisit it, never acted on without the owner. The queries a run report raises are reviewed at receive. A query still below high confidence after review is split into separately tagged parts; packed queries are unpacked before an unattended window. After a Summary that lists open queries, and on request, the interactive pass asks exactly one decision at a time, each query in two replies, and logs and reads back each answer before the next. (standards-queries.md#query-review, standards-queries.md#interactive-pass)
  - _Evidence scope:_ Coordinator summaries, discussion files and review-run reports the owner selects for review.
  - _Review prompt:_ Did every medium- or low-confidence query, and every high-confidence query with a destructive course, pass one blind review run before it reached the owner, did the run see the query without its recommendation or confidence, with the review-independence sentence and earlier decisions stated as dated facts, does each agreed query show its lifted confidence with a reason beginning `reviewed`, or, where the agreement rests only on precedent or only on how the coordinator framed it, its unchanged confidence with a reason beginning `reviewed, precedent only`, does each disputed one keep its confidence and show both views, and does each challenge to an earlier decision end the Context with an option to revisit it?
  - _Outcomes:_ conforming; review the query; show both views; escalate to owner
  - _Conforming guidance:_ Hold an unreviewed query back from the owner until one blind review run has seen it, then mark it reviewed with its lifted confidence, or with its unchanged confidence and `reviewed, precedent only` where the agreement rests only on precedent or framing, or show both views, and show any challenge at the end of the Context with an option to revisit it; never raise a destructive course resting on claims not verified directly to high.
